text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission suggested special measures to restore confidence in the slumping Bulgarian lev, including a possible introduction of a currency board like did Lithuania, Estonia and Argentina.

-- Some 3.339 million Bulgarians voted at the second round of presidential elections on Sunday with 2.040 million of them supporting the opposition candidate Petar Stoyanov and 1.299 million voting for the candidate of the ruling Socialists Ivan Marazov, a Central Electoral Committee spokeswoman said.
-- Bulgaria's deputy premier Rumen Gechev will ask for some $100 million emergency funding from the European Union at a seminar on investment opportunities in Bulgaria in Brussels.

-- The Agricultural Bank of Greece offered a $10 million participation in the projected capital rise of Bulgaria's troubled Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC), BAC executive director Yonka Kinova said.
Bulgaria's central bank acquired for free 51.93 percent stake in BAC in March.

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) board was expected to discuss on Tuesday and Wednesday the bank's strategy for Bulgaria, the newspaper said withoiut quoting sources. A EBRD special mission was expected to arrive in Bulgaria at the end of November, it said.
-- Bulgaria's central bank foreign currency reserves rose by some $35 million in October to $541 million.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) leader Ivan Kostov said that the office of the UDF presidential candidate Petar Stoyanov at the UDF headquarters had been bugged by the Interior Ministry during the campaign.
Officials from the Chief Prosecutor's Office and the Interior Ministry denied the allegation.

-- The ruling Socialist party will evaluate the results of the presidential poll and the cabinet's social and economic policy at a special meeting of its Supreme Council on November 11, a senior party official said.

-- The former deputy director of Bulgaria's private First East International Bank (FEIB) Goran Goranov was arrested on charges of siphoning some $1.3 million FEIB's money to the private Beta Rab company in 1994.
Goranov, who is a shareholder in Beta Rab, was dismissed from the FEIB's board in February 1995.
